findings.summary: docs/ontology.toml exists in the base, so rule (d) runs live. The plan treats it as skipped and never defines what Source::Docs watches.
findings.evidence: Glob finds docs/ontology.toml in the snapshot. It defines terms such as planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed and Sri. Their sources are BRIEF.md, docs/design/job-planning.md, docs/records.md, docs/design/roadmap.md, docs/design/strategy-view.md and docs/design/native-pr-landing.md (ontology.toml lines 36-138). crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs:436 reads the file, and claim_problems (312-433) already checks its content. Yet the plan's dependents entry says the file 'does not exist in the base snapshot; read only by rule (d), skipped while absent', and the risk analysis never treats the ontology entry as a source of send-backs. Mirror::watches is defined for Globs, Path and GitHead, but not for Docs. The files the ontology scans are BRIEF.md plus each term's file sources (scanned_files, ontology.rs 249-257), which only the ontology's own data can tell. A static list would miss sources or catch unrelated files. Fix: Correct the dependents entry: the file exists, and rule (d) runs on the real file in the_real_repo_has_no_mirror_drift and in the producer loop. Define Source::Docs watches as docs/ontology.toml, BRIEF.md and every file source listed in the parsed ontology (reuse scanned_files), and add a unit test for it. Add a loop or check_all test: a producer edits BRIEF.md to add an identifying line such as '- Hermes: ...' that no sense covers, and the job is sent back. Add the live ontology entry to the false-send-back risk.
findings.location: Dependents: 'ontology content mirror'; Decision 1 (Source::Docs, Mirror::watches); Demonstration 4 test (1)

findings.summary: The touch filter works per registry entry, not per finding. A producer that touches any watched file still gets drift that was already in the base.
findings.evidence: check_all with Some(paths) runs every entry whose mirror or source the paths touch. Rule (a) watches crates/*/tests/*.rs and crates/*/src/lib.rs, which most Rust jobs touch. So a base whose timings already lack a unit would send back any producer that edits some lib.rs. The demonstration tests only touched=[README.md], which touches no watched file. Base drift is rare because CI already runs ci_shards and the ontology test, but the plan's claim of 'never' is stronger than the design. Fix: Either run the touched entries on the base tree too (the snapshot's git can read base files) and report only findings that are new, or soften the claim to 'only entries whose files the producer touched'. Add a test where the producer edits crates/demo/tests/a.rs while a b.rs timing line was already missing at the base, and state the expected result.
findings.location: Decision 1 reason ('never with drift already in the base'); Risks (touch filter); Demonstration 3 untouched-drift case

summary: The plan is mostly sound, and I read the snapshot to check it. One central claim is wrong: docs/ontology.toml exists. These claims hold: BUILD_PATHS has five roots (status.rs:20). All nine athena-bin keys in ci.yml hash nine globs. snapshot.base() returns Option<&str>, and producer_loop's self-check is at producer.rs 285-423 as the plan cites. The uncovered-line loop is at ontology.rs 413-430, and the run/tests.rs helpers exist. athena.toml and docs/system-facts.md are compiled into production code (athena-gate lib.rs:33 BUILTIN_CONFIG, briefs.rs:1671 SYSTEM_FACTS), so making the rule two-way and adding the four roots fixes a real problem. On the ontology file: it exists in the base snapshot with seven terms, and ontology.rs already checks its content. The plan says the file is absent, so rule (d) would be skipped in the real-repo test and in the producer loop. In fact the rule will run live. Its touch filter (Mirror::watches for Source::Docs) is never defined, and the set of files it should watch comes from the ontology's own data. That is a wrong dependents entry on a path the plan treats as inert, so I rate it major. The plan also overstates the touch filter: it filters by entry, not by finding, so a producer that touches any file a rule watches still gets drift that was already in the base. That one is minor. Athena's scope findings (files outside the deliverables) are each justified in decision 10, and I do not repeat them.
